The reset theorem assumes iteration<rounds; it does not assert an active transition after halt. pendingJobs exposes the collector pending array and is empty in the halted phase.

Literal and prefix factories override only the prefix flag. They share initialization and the first K-1 estimator rounds on the same private seed and oracle tape. The selector lies in Fin K for K>0, so it chooses x0 through x(K-1) and never needs the literal final estimator round. eventLimit is independent of the prefix flag and covers the literal run too. Therefore the selected points agree pathwise for N>=eventLimit, while the prefix clock is no larger. Their clocks are not equated; final-round cost remains in literal target analyses. cost_composition states measurability of the actual final clock and its nonnegative integral. Actual elapsed time is initialization plus one increment for each of rounds(q) invocations. The eventwise conditional full and difference bounds combine with fresh Bernoulli branch probabilities to give Cfull+rounds*(rho*Cfull+(1-rho)*4*t(S)). Only the second conclusion assumes largeSample, replacing Cfull by 5*t(m). It remains valid for arbitrary positive S and both execution modes. No completed-label scheduling independence or smoothness is needed solely for elapsed time. Zero/infinite advertised times use ENNReal integration; finite clock expectation is not assumed.

scheduled_page_law states equality of the JOINT law of the entire Fin K iterate/estimator prefix and output index, then equality of the actual executed selected-point law with canonical idealOutput. It is not a claim inferred from separate marginal laws. Finite transition induction uses the initial exact pair and the conditional transition identity. The selector coordinate is independent in seedLaw and is never read by queries, collector control or estimator updates; only the selected-output register reads it. Thus the joint selector conclusion is justified without restricting the original oracle tape to a finite or independent-call law. The canonical seed has finite support, hence every squared-gradient quantity at its finite set of selected points is integrable. For actual execution, RegularObjective with nonnegative objective smoothness gives a continuous gradient, so the squared-gradient map is measurable. The joint/output HasLaw statement transports that finite integral to the actual product of algorithm and arbitrary oracle tape laws. The proof must establish this correspondence; no integrability or rate conclusion is added to admissibility.
